title: Fermentation Start Lag After Pitch
app: Brewfather batch exports, iSpindel and Tilt hydrometers, ESPHome mash probes, keg pressure sensors, brew-fridge telemetry, and cellar climate data via MQTT and Splunk HEC.
spl:
index=personal sourcetype=brew:fermentation
| stats avg(hours_to_active) as avg_hours_to_active by batch_name yeast
| where avg_hours_to_active>24
| sort - avg_hours_to_active
description: Uses Fermentation start telemetry telemetry to monitor how long batches take to show active fermentation after pitching in index=personal.
value: Splunk turns the feed into an operational check for laggy starts that might point to yeast or temperature issues, so the signal does not stay buried inside separate consumer apps or exports.
implementation: Ingest Fermentation start telemetry data through its real API, export, MQTT bridge, or open-source connector into `index=personal`; preserve the fields referenced in the SPL and schedule the search on a daily cadence.
visualization: Batch table of average hours to activity.
grandmaExplanation: It flags how long batches take to show active fermentation after pitching so you can spot laggy starts that might point to yeast or temperature issues before it becomes annoying.
